findings.evidence: "9,500/7.08 ≈ 1,342 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20 [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]" and "7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode"
findings.issue: Chapter 5 Table 5-2 uses a 6.0 s decode duration for the ~242,000 tokens/$ row, derived from a 20 ms/token rate (300 × 0.020 = 6.0 s), which is internally consistent. However, on the same page (p.112, §5.3.2), the reconciliation note states "~85% of 7.08 s on the illustrative 20 ms/token basis, where 7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode; ~87% of 8.58 s on the canonical 25 ms/token basis." The 85% figure (6.0/7.08 = 84.7%) and 87% figure (7.5/8.58 = 87.4%) both check out arithmetically. However, the text elsewhere in Ch 4 (p.86) states "~87% of the ~8.58 s window: 7.5 ÷ 8.58 = 87.4%" as the decode wall-clock share without qualifying it as operating-point-dependent in the same way. These are not contradictions per se, but Ch 5's note that "the two percentages are decode shares at two different operating points and should not be compared as if they were one series" is an unusual defensive clarification that suggests the author recognized potential confusion. This is borderline and may not be a true defect.
findings.fix_instruction: If considered a defect: add a cross-reference in Ch 4 §3 (p.86) pointing to Ch 5's reconciliation note so the reader sees the two operating points are explicitly distinguished there too.

findings.evidence: "Output tokens per dollar (single-stream decode, 50 tok/s) | 9,000 output tokens per dollar | 50 tok/s × 3600 s/hr ÷ $20/hr [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]"
findings.issue: Table 5-2's label says 'output tokens per dollar' but the derivation (50 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20 = 9,000) computes tokens/$ for a generic single-stream rate. The 50 tok/s rate is described as a 'single-stream decode' rate, so it does represent output tokens/s, making the label technically correct. However, the row directly below it, 'Total tokens per dollar (overlapped continuous-batching illustration)' computes 50 × (1 + 9,200/300) ≈ 1,583 tok/s, mixing input prefill tokens and output decode tokens in a single 'total tokens' figure. This mixed numerator (input+output tokens at different rates) is not clearly distinguished in the row label from the pure output-only row above. The §5.3 note (p.109) does address basis differences, so this is partially mitigated.
findings.fix_instruction: In Table 5-2 row 'Total tokens per dollar (overlapped continuous-batching illustration)', change label to 'Total (input+output) tokens per dollar' to distinguish from the output-only row above.

findings.evidence: "Total tokens per dollar (same serial floor, no overlap; canonical 25 ms/token basis) | ~199,000 tokens per dollar | 9,500/8.58 ≈ 1,107 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20"
findings.issue: 9,500/8.58 = 1,107.2... ≈ 1,107. Correct. 1,107 × 3600 = 3,985,200. 3,985,200/20 = 199,260 ≈ 199,000. Correct (rounded to 3 significant figures). Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "Total tokens per dollar (overlapped continuous-batching illustration) | ~285,000 tokens per dollar at 300 output tokens/request | 50 × (1 + 9,200/300) ≈ 1,583 tok/s × 3600 ÷ $20"
"the prefill leg consumes ~97% of the tokens per request (9,200 ÷ 9,500)"
findings.issue: 9,200/9,500 = 0.9684 = 96.8%. The text says '~97%'. 96.8% rounds to 97%. Correct. The text then says 'and, because each prefill token runs the full 2 × 70B forward FLOP, it is also ~97% of the linear forward-FLOP cost (before the quadratic attention term)'. This is correct: if all tokens run the same 2N FLOP per token, the FLOP share equals the token share. Arithmetic verified — no defect.

findings.evidence: "~85% of 7.08 s on the illustrative 20 ms/token basis, where 7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode"
findings.issue: 6.0/7.08 = 0.8475 = 84.7%. The text says '~85%'. 84.7 rounds to 85. Correct. And: '~87% of 8.58 s on the canonical 25 ms/token basis, where 8.58 s = 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode'. 7.5/8.58 = 0.8741 = 87.4%. The text says '~87%'. 87.4 rounds to 87. Correct. Arithmetic verified — no defect.
